plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, clump-forming perennial with hairy stems and abundant daisy-like flower heads with yellow centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies and many native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, widely cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Its flowers close at night and on cloudy days, and the plant is a key food stop for monarch butterflies on their autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In spring the blossoms carpet streets and parks with purple petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earn it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and a falling bloom on your head is said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like pink-lilac flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The leaves appear the following spring, then die back before the next flowering.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges across Europe, from the UK to the Balkans
plants.funFact: Although it looks like a crocus, it is a member of the lily family and is highly toxic, yet it is the source of colchicine, a medicine used to treat gout.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with feathery foliage and saucer-shaped flowers on tall slender stems. It thrives in full sun and poor soil, and continues blooming until the first frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost (June to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Mexico; cultivated in gardens across the world
plants.funFact: The name 'cosmos' comes from the Greek word for 'harmony' or 'ordered universe', and cosmos seeds have even been grown aboard the International Space Station.
